location: Boundaries > Always (Phase timings) + Design Notes; cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields / Phase timings
issue: The record has one flat `wall_clock` field (Fields list). Phase timings gives the boot its own wall_clock ('boot_phases with the boot's own wall_clock') and also defines the cell's `wall_clock` as finished_at minus started_at. Aggregate `e2e_phase_durations.boots[<boot_id>].wall_clock` needs the boot value from each record. No field name for the boot wall-clock exists except inside `keeper_boot`. The spec's child list ('per-engine cells + boot_phases, wall_clock') does not say which one `wall_clock` is.
implementation_impact: The implementer has to invent where the boot wall-clock lives: overwrite the cell's wall_clock, nest it in boot_phases, or add a new field. Aggregate, tests and the bankwire timing report then disagree on what `wall_clock` means.
suggestion: Name both explicitly, for example record `wall_clock` = cell (finished_at - started_at) and `boot_wall_clock` (or `boot_phases` = {phases, wall_clock}). State which one the aggregate reads for `boots` and which for `browsers`.

location: Execution task ps-flashlight-run.py ('make `phase` record `{seconds, outcome}`'); cell-contract.md > Phase timings
issue: `outcome` has no value set and `seconds` has no type. Today `phase.__exit__` writes END statuses 'ok', 'timeout', 'error(<Exc>)', or any free-form `ph.status` ('gagal', 'timeout(sisa-artefak: jalankan --cleanup-orphans)'). `_elapsed()` returns int seconds. Nothing says whether `outcome` copies that string or maps it to an enum, or whether seconds is an int or a float.
implementation_impact: Tests and the aggregate's `e2e_phase_durations` get an unstable shape. Sub-second phases rounded to int read as 0, which undermines 'see whether boot or browser driving dominates'.
suggestion: Define `seconds` as a float (for example monotonic, rounded to 3 decimals) and `outcome` as an enum (ok|timeout|error|failed), with the free-form status kept elsewhere or dropped.

location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-e2e-run.py`: per-engine cells) + I/O row 'Crash child'; cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage / Fields sub-bullet 'engine never started'
issue: When the boot fails (image missing, wait-healthy timeout, install failure, wait-http unreachable), today's `run_one_version` returns early with version-level `errors` and no per-engine data. Storage says ps-run-layer writes `crash` 'when the child left none'. So unless the child emits a `cells` entry for every engine even when no engine started, an install failure becomes a `crash` record instead of reason `install`/`errors`. The sub-bullet also says such cells get `started_at` = 'when ps-run-layer admitted it', which the child cannot know. Nothing says who builds these records.
implementation_impact: Two plausible implementations produce different reasons for the same infra failure. Infra-cause classification later (blocked-infra) and the I/O 'Crash child' test both depend on it.
suggestion: State that the child always emits `cells.<engine>` for every requested engine on every path after the probe, with `started_at`/`finished_at` null when the engine never started. ps-run-layer then fills started_at/finished_at (its spawn time and its write time) for those cells and for crash records.

location: I/O row 'Probe drop'; Boundaries > Always (ps-run-layer record merge + crash/browser-unavailable records); cell-contract.md > Storage
issue: ps-run-layer must write `browser-unavailable` for 'an engine the binary probe dropped', but the probe runs inside the child (`main`: `usable = [e for e in requested if browser_available(e)]`). The spec does not say which child output field tells ps-run-layer that an engine was probe-dropped rather than lost to a crash. Today the candidates are top-level `browsers_available`, the version-level `browser_notes` text, and `skipped_browser`.
implementation_impact: Without a defined signal, ps-run-layer either parses free-text notes or labels every missing engine `crash`, which breaks the 'Probe drop' row.
suggestion: Specify the signal, for example a child top-level `browsers_available` list or `cells.<engine> = {"state": "inconclusive", "reason": "browser-unavailable"}` emitted by the child. State that ps-run-layer maps a missing engine to `browser-unavailable` only when that signal says so, and to `crash` otherwise.

location: Boundaries > Always ('exit 3/1/0/2/143 per Runner', 'Runner > Output JSON line') vs Never ('not-run production' deferred); cell-contract.md > Runner > Output
issue: Runner > Output, which the spec imports, says a child exit 2 'stops queued cells as fail-fast does (`not-run`, reason `input-error after <ver>`), in-flight children finish, and ps-run-layer exits 2'. The spec defers not-run production (CAP-3). It does not say what replaces it: whether the other versions' already-finished child results are still appended, whether queued children still start, or whether the tmp dir is kept as `collect()`'s `rejected` path does today.
implementation_impact: The child-exit-2 path is undefined in history mode. One implementation drops valid evidence from sibling versions, another appends it, and a third leaves orphan queued children running.
suggestion: Define the interim behaviour: on the first child exit 2, start no further queued child, let in-flight children finish, append their records, append nothing for unstarted cells, and exit 2. Add a test.

location: Boundaries > Always (ps-run-layer e2e history mode); cell-contract.md > Storage ('when the child left none')
issue: Not covered: a child output that parses but fails today's checks in history mode. Today `collect()` rejects stray versions (exit 2) and `validate_layer_shape` failures exit 2 with the tmp dir kept. The contract only distinguishes a 'per-cell result' from 'none'. Also undefined: a payload whose `cells` lacks an admitted engine that was not probe-dropped, a payload with an extra engine, or `cells` present but malformed.
implementation_impact: The implementer must decide between exit 2 (no records, tmp kept) and `crash` records for each malformed shape, and the shape gate before merge may be dropped or kept arbitrarily.
suggestion: List the outcomes: stray version or engine → exit 2 with tmp kept and nothing appended for that version; unparseable or shape-invalid output → `crash` for each admitted cell; missing engine not probe-dropped → `crash`.

location: Boundaries > Always (ps-run-layer exit 143); Never ('`stopped` records' deferred); cell-contract.md > Storage
issue: When ps-run-layer is stopped via `--stop-job` (JobStopped raised in its main thread, `_run()` returns 143), the contract appends a `stopped` record for each admitted cell. The spec defers `stopped` records without saying what to do instead: append nothing, append `crash`, or append results of children that already finished before the signal.
implementation_impact: A stop mid-run could silently lose evidence that finished, or write `crash` records that later count toward the deferred blocked-infra rule.
suggestion: State explicitly: on stop, append records only for children that already exited with a result, append nothing for in-flight or unstarted cells, print no output line, and exit 143.

location: Boundaries > Always ('`ready` false unless every configured cell...' and Runner input errors); cell-contract.md > Runner > Input errors
issue: The spec imports exit codes 'per Runner', but the contract's Runner input-error list mixes in-scope and deferred rules. In scope: neither/both of --cells/--versions; version repeated in --cells; cell outside the configured set; --per-version; psm_reports_dir equal to the module root; passthrough --screenshot-dir inside the module but outside psm_reports_dir; --cells with another layer. Contradicted or deferred: '--tier missing or other than 0/1' (spec: no --tier, tier null), '--jobs' is exit 2 (spec: --jobs stays), '--warm/--scenarios-from-failed'. The spec names only cells/versions and --per-version.
implementation_impact: The implementer must guess which input errors to enforce. Enforcing '--tier missing' would make every e2e run exit 2, and skipping the reports-dir/screenshot-dir checks lets screenshots written into the module stale the run's own fingerprint.
suggestion: Enumerate the exact exit-2 cases for this slice, and state that --tier and --jobs are not checked (--jobs keeps bounding concurrent versions).

location: Boundaries > Always (Plan's per-cell `rerun_matrix` and browser-keyed `layers.e2e`, 'both modes'); ps-plan-layers.py main canonical branch
issue: Canonical mode has no `rerun_matrix` today (only `layers` + `rerun`; `per_version_rollup` runs only for --per-version). The contract says canonical `layers.e2e` is 'keyed by browser' and that `rerun` lists e2e while 'any configured cell has an e2e rerun_matrix entry'. It is undefined whether canonical mode gains a `rerun_matrix`, and what a browser-keyed canonical `layers.e2e[browser]` value means across three versions (reuse only if all versions pass? per-version nested?).
implementation_impact: Two incompatible output shapes are possible, and tests or docs written against one break the other. The I/O row 'Narrowed plan' does not say which mode it covers.
suggestion: Specify the canonical shape exactly, for example `layers.e2e = {<browser>: {<ver>: {reuse, reason, path}}}` plus a top-level `rerun_matrix` in both modes. State the per-version `layers.e2e[browser]` value shape too.

location: Boundaries > Always (Plan rerun_matrix for every configured cell) vs Never (`phase1_reuse` deferred, CAP-1); references/run-phases.md Fase 1 ('`all_reuse` adalah gerbangnya')
issue: The contract makes e2e `rerun_matrix` entries cover every configured cell whatever --versions, and keeps `all_reuse` 'today's computation' (`not matrix`). It says the real gates are `phase1_reuse` and `e2e_step`, both deferred here. Today Fase 1 for version V is gated on `all_reuse` of a `--versions V --per-version` plan. With this slice, any stale e2e cell of another version keeps `all_reuse` false, so V's Phase 1 loop can never end. The contract rule depends on the deferred `phase1_reuse` and the spec gives no replacement.
implementation_impact: The documented Phase 1 loop either never terminates or the docs writer invents a gate. It also matters whether `all_reuse` is computed over the matrix (all cells) or over the per-version `rerun` lists (requested versions only).
suggestion: State the interim Phase 1 gate (for example 'V's `per_version[V].rerun` is empty') and whether `all_reuse` counts out-of-scope e2e cells. Update run-phases.md accordingly.

location: Boundaries > Never (headless config copy deferred); cell-contract.md > Headless + Configured cells; SPEC.md > Constraints (headless callers keep per-version verdict)
issue: The contract keeps headless callers working because they write their versions and browsers into a config copy that becomes the configured set. This slice defers that copy but makes the configured set (from --config, resolver defaults 3×2) the only source of `ready`. A headless caller (psm-develop or psm-cross-version validating only 9.1) therefore always gets `ready=false` and `versions[1.7.8/8.1].ready=false`, a regression of its per-version verdict contract. The spec says nothing about this interim behaviour.
implementation_impact: Shipping this slice breaks every headless caller's readiness signal until the CAP-1 headless slice lands, or the implementer improvises a config copy that the spec forbids ('do not half-build').
suggestion: Decide the interim: either include the minimal headless config copy (`psm_target_versions`/`psm_e2e_browsers` written from caller args) in this slice, or state explicitly that headless callers get ready=false for unrequested versions and update headless.md and caller SKILL.md files to read only their versions' `versions[ver]`.

location: Execution task 'docs' (SKILL.md Fase 1/2 e2e commands, run-phases.md); Never (tiers, `e2e_next_cells`, `e2e_step` deferred)
issue: The contract's orchestration (run exactly `e2e_next_cells`, loop while `e2e_step` is gate, wrap-up) is deferred, but `--per-version` for e2e becomes exit 2 and `--browsers` becomes reserved. The spec gives no interim Fase 1/Fase 2 recipe: which cells each phase runs (`--versions V` = all configured browsers? the e2e `rerun_matrix` cells grouped into `--cells`?), when Fase 2 starts, and whether `--merge-only --layer e2e` stays gated by `all_reuse`.
implementation_impact: The docs writer must design the interim workflow. Two writers would produce different command sequences, and the documented flow could re-run passing cells or never re-require Firefox.
suggestion: Add a short interim recipe: Fase 1 = `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --versions V --session <t> --config …` when V's plan lists e2e; Fase 2 = `--cells` built from the e2e `rerun_matrix` entries; then `--merge-only --layer e2e` (no all_reuse gate) and the aggregate.

location: Execution task 'docs' (e2e-quickstart.md TDD verdict step); cell-contract.md > Docs to update
issue: The contract's quickstart verdict step is `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --cells … --tier 0 --session <token>`, but this slice adds no `--tier` flag. argparse would reject it with exit 2. The aggregate also needs `--module`, `--config` and a static file to produce a verdict. The spec does not give the slice's form.
implementation_impact: Copying the contract's command into the docs produces a command that fails. Leaving out --config or the static input gives a misleading verdict.
suggestion: Give the exact quickstart commands for this slice (no --tier; `--new-session` first; `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir … --module … --config …`).

location: Boundaries > Always (State, freshness, gate-grade; Plan reasons; Aggregate reasons) vs Never (CAP-1 Plan derivation)
issue: Several in-scope rules depend on definitions in the deferred Plan derivation paragraph. Reason `not-gradeable` uses 'not-gradeable (below)' with authored_assertions 0, or scenario_notes equal to the plan's current `e2e_scenario_notes`. The aggregate reason `stale-fail` applies 'when the cell is failing (Plan)'. Per-version `e2e_state` uses 'newest gate-grade record is fail'. The spec does not say these definitions are in scope, or that 'failing' and 'not-gradeable' must be implemented while steps, focus and tiers are not.
implementation_impact: The implementer may skip `not-gradeable`/`stale-fail` as CAP-1 material, or half-build the derivation. Either way, reasons differ from the contract.
suggestion: List explicitly that the 'failing' and 'not-gradeable' predicates from Plan are in scope (as functions), while steps, focus, tiers and next cells are not.

location: Boundaries > Always (Aggregate reasons 'as in the plan'); cell-contract.md > Aggregate + Plan reasons `scenario-notes`/`not-gradeable`
issue: The plan's `scenario-notes` vs `not-gradeable` split compares a record's `scenario_notes` with the *current* `e2e_scenario_notes`, which the plan derives live via `discover_scenarios` (including git-derived `deleted_specs`). The contract says the aggregate's `e2e_scenario_notes` 'comes from the selected records only'. So the aggregate has no 'current' notes to compare against, yet its reasons must match the plan's.
implementation_impact: The aggregate and the plan can report different reasons for the same cell, or the implementer adds a live discover_scenarios/git call to the aggregate that the contract does not mention.
suggestion: State whether the aggregate computes current notes live (and with which module path), or define its reason computation without that comparison.

location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate (`e2e_cells`, `versions[ver].reason`), referenced by Boundaries > Always
issue: `e2e_cells[ver][browser] = {state, gate_grade, reason, findings, parallel_only}` has no defined `state` for a configured cell with no record (`missing`) or whose only lines are corrupt. `versions[ver].reason` is a single value, but a version has several cells, each possibly with a different reason. Nothing says which cell's reason wins, or whether it is a list or joined string.
implementation_impact: The aggregate output shape is guessed, and acceptance criterion 2 ('e2e_cells names it with a contract reason') can be satisfied by several incompatible shapes.
suggestion: Define: missing/corrupt cell → `state: null` (or 'missing'), `gate_grade: false`, `findings: []`. Define `versions[ver].reason` as either the first cell in browser order or a `{<browser>: reason}` map.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan reasons (`stale-tag`, `stale-source` (no fresh record))
issue: When no record is fresh, the reason is `stale-tag` or `stale-source`, but the spec does not say which record decides it: the newest record, any record, or a record whose fingerprint matches but whose tag differs. A history with an old record on the current fingerprint but an old tag, and a newer record on an old fingerprint, has no defined answer.
implementation_impact: Reasons become implementation-dependent, and tests asserting a specific stale reason are fragile.
suggestion: Define it: judge from the newest valid record; `stale-tag` when its fingerprint matches but its tag differs, else `stale-source`.

location: Execution task ps-plan-layers.py (`record_state`); cell-contract.md > State + incomplete-record rule
issue: Records carry a stored `state` and `conclusive`, while State defines state from fields (not driven, errors, install.ok, launch_error, findings). The incomplete-record rule makes readers override a stored pass/fail. It is not said whether readers recompute state from the fields for every record (a stored `pass` with non-empty findings would read as `fail`) or trust the stored `state` except for the incomplete-record downgrade. 'Engine not driven' has no record-level test either.
implementation_impact: Writer and reader can disagree, and `record_state` may be built as a pure reader of `state` or as a recomputation. That gives different results on legacy or hand-edited lines.
suggestion: State that ps-run-layer computes `state`/`conclusive`/`reason` at merge time, and that readers apply only the corrupt and incomplete-record rules (or the reverse). Define 'not driven' (for example `started_at` set by ps-run-layer and no `browser:<engine>` phase).

location: Boundaries > Always (Producers 'as written'); cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Producers ('Each finding gains `action` and `step`')
issue: The contract requires each finding to carry `action` and `step` (the 0-based index in the spec's `steps`). `run_steps`/`_res` results today carry no step index, and `assemble_findings` emits id/severity/message/location/browser/scenario/source/versions only. Neither the spec's ps-e2e-run task nor the Code Map mentions this change, which touches `run_steps` and the universal smoke.
implementation_impact: The change is easy to miss, and the later CAP-7 identical-findings comparison key (version, browser, scenario, step, action) has no data.
suggestion: Add the item to the ps-e2e-run.py task: carry the step index through `run_steps` results into `assemble_findings` (`action`, `step`), and add a test.

location: Boundaries > Always (ps-e2e-run.py child fields); cell-contract.md > Fields / Producers
issue: The spec's child field list leaves out several contract fields: `scenarios_run` (spec `name` list), version-level `image_tag` (today the field is `tag`), and the null hooks `keeper_boot`, `scenario_spans`, `parallel_only`. 'keep hooks null/absent' does not say whether a field is written as null or omitted. It is also unclear whether the Fields list is closed (drop `boot_log`, `ps_domain`, `orchestrator`, `skipped_image`) or open.
implementation_impact: Record shapes differ between implementations, and fixtures in tests must guess. A later slice that treats absent and null differently could misread these records.
suggestion: Give the exact record key set for this slice: fields present with null for deferred hooks, `scenarios_run` = names of the full set run, `image_tag` renamed from `tag`, and whether extra fields are kept.

location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-plan-layers.py --new-session`; plan and aggregate accept `--session` optionally) vs cell-contract.md > Fields ('passed as --session to every plan call ... both reject a missing or malformed token')
issue: The contract requires `--session` on every plan call (missing → exit 2). The spec makes it optional for the plan. That is a contract change, not a deferral, and the frontmatter's 'Ask First: changing any contract rule' is not acknowledged. Separately, the spec says `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` requires `--session` unconditionally, while the contract exempts `--merge-only --layer e2e` ('--session do not apply').
implementation_impact: An implementer following the spec literally rejects `--merge-only --layer e2e` without --session. One following the contract rejects plan calls without --session, and existing docs or tests break.
suggestion: State that --session is optional for the plan in this slice, as a deliberate deviation, and that `--merge-only --layer e2e` neither requires nor accepts --session.

location: Boundaries > Always (configured cells; `ps-run-layer.py --config` for every layer, `--config`/`--browsers`/`--engines` join RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH); SKILL.md On Activation step 2
issue: The interactive scope menu narrows browsers via `--browsers` passed to every layer. After this slice, `--browsers` in ps-run-layer passthrough is exit 2, plan `--browsers` is deferred, and `--versions` for e2e always means all configured browsers. The spec's docs task does not cover SKILL.md On Activation step 2, so the documented way to narrow browsers breaks. Existing `-- --config …` passthrough usage (run-phases.md 'Teruskan --config … ke Lapis 1/2/4') also becomes exit 2.
implementation_impact: The interactive flow gives an exit-2 error on its first narrowed E2E run, and the docs writer has to invent the replacement (`--cells`).
suggestion: Add SKILL.md On Activation step 2 to the docs task: browser narrowing maps to `--cells`, and --config moves from passthrough to a ps-run-layer flag. Also update the ps-run-layer docstring example, which passes `--browsers` after `--`.

location: cell-contract.md > Runner > Input errors ('RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH (prefix abbreviations included)'); ps-run-layer.py `reserved_in_passthrough`
issue: Today abbreviation detection is hard-coded to four flags ('--versions', '--output', '--progress-file', '--job-id'), with a minimum length of 4. The contract requires prefix abbreviations for every reserved flag. The spec adds `--config`, `--browsers`, `--engines` to the tuple but does not say the abbreviation loop must cover them. Short prefixes such as `--con` or `--br` collide with legitimate child flags (`--conf…` vs `--config`).
implementation_impact: A literal implementation adds the names to the tuple only, so `--brow chromium` or `--conf x.json` slips through to the child and overrides ps-run-layer's own value.
suggestion: State that the abbreviation check iterates over all of RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH, and define the ambiguity rule (match argparse's unique-prefix behaviour against the child's parser).

location: Boundaries > Always (Configured cells; Bad config row); Execution task ps-flashlight-run.py (configured-cells reader)
issue: The normalizer's input format is undefined. Resolver values are comma-separated strings ('1.7.8,8.1,9.1'), but a hand-written config may hold a JSON list. The spec also does not say whether whitespace or case is tolerated ('Chromium'), whether a config present without the key falls back to script defaults, or whether `--versions` of ps-run-layer (e2e) must match configured strings exactly, as `--cells` and the canary do.
implementation_impact: Exit-2 behaviour differs between scripts, and the 'Bad config' test cannot be written unambiguously.
suggestion: Specify: accept a string (comma-split, strip, lowercase engines) or a list of strings. A missing key → script default. `--versions` for e2e must match a configured string exactly, else exit 2.

location: Boundaries > Always (State, freshness: `source_fingerprint`); cell-contract.md > Fresh
issue: Fingerprint details are open. 'Every file' does not say whether symlinks (lstat entry, not followed) and directories, including empty ones, are entries. 'Top-level `.psm-*` files' does not say whether `.psm-*` directories are covered. `psm_reports_dir` is undefined for the plan and aggregate when no --config is given, and the plan's default `--reports-dir` is the relative `_bmad-output/psm-validate`. The 'reports dir equal to module root' error is assigned to the Runner only, leaving plan and aggregate behaviour undefined.
implementation_impact: Plan, runner and aggregate can compute different fingerprints for the same tree, which makes every record read stale. The shared-function rule mitigates this only if all callers pass the same exclusion path.
suggestion: Define the entry set (regular files and symlinks as lstat entries, no directories) and the exclusion (`realpath(--reports-dir)` when strictly inside the module). Make reports dir = module root exit 2 in all three scripts.

location: Execution task ps-e2e-run.py ('boot timing wrapper measured after teardown') + Design Notes
issue: The start point of the boot wall-clock is undefined: before the image-present check and `pull`, or at `bring-up`. Also unspecified: what the boot fields are when no boot happened (compose unavailable or skipped_image before bring-up) — empty `boot_phases` {} or null — and whether `boot_id` is still set. The port-conflict retry also yields `bring-up#2` and an extra `teardown`, which the spec does not mention.
implementation_impact: Boot wall-clock numbers in the success-signal timing report depend on an arbitrary choice. Null/empty handling differs between child and aggregate.
suggestion: Define it: the boot wall-clock spans from the image check (including pull) to the end of teardown. No container started → `boot_phases` {} (or null) and `boot_id` still the RUN_ID. Retries follow the #n rule.

location: Boundaries > Always (Aggregate `--config`, versions replace `--versions`); cell-contract.md > Aggregate
issue: 'A `--versions` that differs is an input error' does not define 'differs' (set, order, or string form such as 9.1 vs 9.1.0). The aggregate's E2E history reading needs `--reports-dir` + `--module`, and the spec does not say what happens when the aggregate is called with explicit `--static` and no `--reports-dir` (all cells `missing`, or exit 2). `e2e_screenshot_dir` = 'distinct run folders of the selected records' screenshots' requires deriving the `run-<ts>` ancestor from file paths, which is not specified.
implementation_impact: Edge-case behaviour is guessed, and tests for the removed `unscanned` gate and the new versions source are underspecified.
suggestion: Define 'differs' as set inequality after normalization. Require `--reports-dir`+`--module` for E2E (exit 2 otherwise, or all cells missing). Define the run folder as the first ancestor matching `run-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`.

location: Execution task 'tests' ('contract-named tests in scope')
issue: 'Contract-named tests in scope' is not enumerated, and some contract tests straddle deferred pieces. The Configured-cells test ('config 3×2 plus `--versions 9.1 --browsers chromium` still lists the other five cells as rerun') needs plan `--browsers`, which is deferred. The gate-grade test ('pass then fail ... gives ready=false and a step other than done') needs `e2e_step`, also deferred.
implementation_impact: The implementer must decide which assertions to drop or adapt. A reviewer cannot check completeness.
suggestion: List the exact tests for this slice, and give the adapted form of the two straddling tests (`--versions 9.1` only; assert reason `fail` instead of step).

location: Execution task ps-flashlight-run.py ('move `SUPPORTED_ENGINES`'); tests/test-ps-flashlight-run.py drift test
issue: The spec moves `SUPPORTED_ENGINES` but does not say where the configured-cells defaults (`chromium,firefox`, `1.7.8,8.1,9.1`) live. The existing anti-drift test reads `DEFAULT_BROWSERS` from ps-e2e-run.py via ast and compares it to `PSM_DEFAULTS['psm_e2e_browsers']`. If the shared normalizer or reader owns the defaults, the test either silently guards a dead constant or breaks.
implementation_impact: The single-owner rule for defaults is easy to violate, leaving two copies that can drift.
suggestion: Say where the default browser and version lists live after the move, and update the drift test to read that owner.

location: Acceptance Criteria 1 + Boundaries > Always (Honesty law)
issue: Criterion 1 asserts that `ready` 'holds the E2E part true', but `ready` is a single boolean that also needs static conclusiveness (`version_ready` floor) and every `--require` layer. 'Counts each boot_id once' is trivially true of a dict keyed by boot_id. The Honesty law in Always says `ready` is false unless every configured cell passes, while the contract keeps `--require` without `e2e` as the way to gate without E2E.
implementation_impact: The criterion is either untestable as worded or passes trivially. The Honesty-law sentence, read literally, contradicts the retained `--require` opt-out.
suggestion: Rephrase criterion 1: with a conclusive static file for the 3 versions and `--require static,e2e`, `ready=true`, and `e2e_phase_durations[ver].boots` has exactly one key per distinct boot_id with the phases from one record. Add 'when `--require` includes e2e' to the Honesty-law line.

location: Boundaries > Always ('Runner > Output' skipped rule); cell-contract.md > Runner > Output ('when `docker_available()` is false before slot counting')
issue: The skipped rule is anchored to 'before slot counting', but slots are deferred. The spec does not say whether ps-run-layer itself probes `docker_available()` before spawning, or relies on children reporting `status: skipped`. Playwright-absent also only shows up from the child.
implementation_impact: Two implementations differ in whether children are spawned without Docker. Output and exit code may differ when some children skip and others crash.
suggestion: State: ps-run-layer calls `fl.docker_available()` before spawning any child; false → print `{e2e_status: skipped, ...}`, append nothing, exit 0. A child's skipped status is handled per the Output rule.

location: Frontmatter `context` list
issue: The spec says it delegates to the contract files, but `context` lists SPEC.md, cell-contract.md and brownfield.md, not tier-matrix.md. tier-matrix.md restates the `ready` definition and the 'empty tier 1 never makes ready true' rule.
implementation_impact: Tooling that loads only `context` misses part of the contract. The impact is low, because the slice's rules are in cell-contract.md.
suggestion: Add tier-matrix.md to `context`, or state that it is out of scope for this slice.

location: Boundaries > Always ('`--per-version` is exit 2', 'writes no <module>-e2e*.json except --merge-only'); ps-plan-layers.py per_version_path / ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir derivation
issue: Existing users have `<module>-e2e-<ver>.json` and `<module>-e2e.json` on disk, and the aggregate's reports-dir derivation auto-picks `<module>-e2e.json` today. The spec says these are ignored but does not say whether the new `--merge-only` view file (same name `<module>-e2e.json`, `view: true`) overwrites a legacy canonical file, or whether the aggregate must skip that name even when `--e2e` is not passed (rather than reject only explicit `--e2e`).
implementation_impact: The aggregate may keep auto-loading the view file through the derivation loop and run it through `validate_layer_shape`/`e2e_layer`. That crashes or produces a wrong verdict.
suggestion: State that the derivation loop in `ps-aggregate.py main` skips layer `e2e` entirely, and that the view write overwrites any legacy file of that name.
